tests.expectation: Resubmitting the same checkout form after it completed creates no second order.
Two overlapping submissions of the same checkout create exactly one order.
Client times out while the server is still processing; the retry results in exactly one order and no server error.
If saving the order fails, nothing is persisted and a retry places exactly one order.
If a failure happens after the order insert but before the customer is told, a retry leaves exactly one order.
After a completed order, a new checkout with the same items creates a second order.
After a completed order, a new checkout with different items creates a second order.
D7: reloading the checkout page while the first submission is still in flight and submitting again is a retry; exactly one order, and (D3) neither submission ends in a server error.
Normal checkout still lands on the confirmation page, persists one order with the basket's units and empties the basket.
Checkout with an empty basket creates no order and no server error.
Duplicate protection does not block or merge different customers' concurrent checkouts.
Retrying a completed checkout shows the order confirmation rather than an error or empty basket.
Neither of two overlapping submissions ends in a server error.
